messages:
ben_support: FYI customer reported timeouts hitting our private inference endpoint from their VPC (private deployment, us-east-1). They see TLS handshake hang then reset. They tried from 2 different subnets. curl output: ```curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer```

irene_eng: thanks — can you share the instance/bastion IP they used and the flow logs/traceroute? usually either SG egress or NACL is blocking ephemeral return ports or TLS termination is being intercepted.

ben_support: bastion IP 10.10.45.12 (customer side). Customer sent a short traceroute: ```traceroute to inference.redwood-private.local (172.31.40.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.45.1  0.4 ms 0.3 ms 0.3 ms
 2  172.31.40.10  * * *``` so they never complete TCP handshake.

ashok_sre: can you run a quick port test from their bastion? `nc -vz 172.31.40.10 443` — also capture a tcpdump on the inference host to see SYNs. If NACLs are blocking ephemeral source ports, we'll see SYN reach then RST or nothing.

ben_support: customer ran `nc -vz` and got: ```nc: connect to 172.31.40.10 port 443 (tcp) failed: Connection refused``` — they also ran `curl --tlsv1.2 -v https://172.31.40.10/` and it shows `* TCP_NODELAY set` then stalls at `* Connected to 172.31.40.10 (172.31.40.10) port 443 (#0)` then `* SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 0 bytes` then `* Connection reset by peer`.

irene_eng: ok, quick theory: NACL on the subnet is stateless. If the customer SG allows outbound 443 but the subnet NACL denies ephemeral ports for inbound (return) traffic, the handshake will fail. SGs are stateful so they don't need special return rules, but NACLs do. Ask them to paste `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxxxx` output or the NACL ID.

ben_support: customer sent NACL id `acl-0a1b2c3d4e` and this excerpt: ```Entries:
 Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 egress true
 Rule 101: DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0 ingress false
 Rule 102: ALLOW TCP 80 0.0.0.0/0 ingress true``` They have a DENY ALL entry ordering after an allow which is odd.

ashok_sre: that DENY ALL with `egress false` is probably the problem — NACLs are evaluated by rule number ascending. If they have a DENY for all inbound (ingress) with a rule number lower/equal to others it will block ephemeral return. Ask for full ordered list.

ben_support: pasted full list (customer): ```100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 egress true
110 DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0 ingress true
120 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0 ingress true``` they said entry 110 was added by their infra team during a lockdown.

irene_eng: aha — rule 110 DENY ALL (ingress) will block the TCP handshake return packets unless there's a higher priority ALLOW that matches earlier. Their later ALLOW 120 is lower priority (higher number) so it never applies. Two fixes: 1) remove/adjust the DENY rule or 2) explicitly add allow for ephemeral ports with a lower rule number than the DENY. Also add corresponding egress rules if needed.

ashok_sre: suggested command to reorder/replace: 
```bash
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d4e --rule-number 110 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow --egress false --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0
```
Note: they can also insert a new lower-numbered ALLOW for 1024-65535 ingress.

ben_support: customer changed NACL: they replaced rule 110 with `ALLOW ALL ingress` as a quick test. After that they see successful TLS handshake. curl now shows `* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / ECDHE...` then response 200.

irene_eng: great — please tell them to follow least-privilege: prefer scoping by source CIDR (their perimeter) and only allow ephemeral port range (1024-65535) for ingress return, and ensure rule numbers are correct (lower numbers evaluated first). Add a note: AWS default ephemeral on some AMIs uses 32768-65535 — but recommended safe range is 1024-65535 to cover all.

ben_support: customer updated to `100 ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0 egress true`, `105 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 10.10.0.0/16 ingress true`, `110 DENY ALL 0.0.0.0/0 ingress true` and they validated connectivity.

netbot: (automatic) added incident tag `vpc-nacl-ephemeral-allow` to thread.

ashok_sre: follow-up action: adding a short KB for Private deployments: checklist for networking test: 
- verify SG egress to endpoint port (443 by default)
- verify NACL ingress allows ephemeral range (1024-65535) or at minimum 32768-65535 depending on OS
- test from customer bastion: `nc -vz <endpoint> 443` and `tcpdump -n -s0 -c50 port 443` on host
- provide sample aws CLI commands to inspect NACL/SG

irene_eng: marking as resolved. ben, can you ask customer to confirm they want their change formalized or prefer we close?

ben_support: customer asked us to keep the change and they will run a follow-up security review. closing in 48h if no regression. :thumbsup:

ashok_sre: noting for postmortem: common trap is adding DENY ALL ingress without ordering consideration. We'll add a short blurb to the Private deployment onboarding doc.

ben_support: closing notes: NACL rule numbers and stateless nature of NACLs are the root cause. Problem resolved after allowing ephemeral port range with proper rule ordering.
